Scope in: glossary/species.json for every species the bank names plus Portaria 67/2024's list; glossary/terms.json for the hunting and legal vocabulary; one translations/en/ file per chunk file, all 506 entries, every entry at status checked by the end; the loader hook wired; pnpm lint and pnpm test green with rules 5 and 6 live.
Scope out: hints (phase 3 epic); status reviewed and any in-app control for it (phase 4 epic); a validator rule that enforces terms in translations; importing or correcting the earlier cacador-quiz English; any edit to questions/ or the extractor.
notes:
**DECISIONS** (epic-scoped log; durable record written to DESIGN.md § 9 in bead .1)

- D1 Translations are written fresh, one agent per group of chunk files, with both glossaries as READ FIRST; the earlier cacador-quiz English is never opened by a worker. Reason: a 39-question sample plus a tally of every species option found it wrong and inconsistent on species (arrabio→teal, pato-trombeteiro→wigeon and goldeneye, narceja-galega→great snipe) and on terms (de salto→jump method, jump hunting, walk-up); fixing it costs as much as redoing it and keeps its anchoring. Record: cac-qgb notes FOUND.
- D2 glossary/species.json holds every species name the bank uses, each surface form (singular and plural) its own entry, plus every species of Portaria 67/2024 (diariodarepublica.pt/dr/detalhe/portaria/67-2024-853384722). group is the manifest topic slug when the species' family has one (patos for every duck, tordos for every thrush, pombos-rolas for pigeons and doves), nao-cinegeticas for a protected species, outras-cinegeticas for a game species with no topic (corvids, starling, geese). Reason: rule 6 already enforces the shape and allows entries the bank never names (DESIGN.md § 4).
- D3 glossary/terms.json, shape { pt, en, note }, pt unique and in the bank's surface form, holds the hunting and legal vocabulary; the validator checks only its shape (new rule 7); its use in translations is checked by the meaning pass, not by a rule. Reason: terms inflect, a rule would be loose or noisy (cac-qgb D3).
- D4 Register is literal-leaning: keep the Portuguese order and structure where English allows, British spelling (licence, metres, colour), numbers, units and times as the Portuguese has them, a bare number or proper name copied unchanged. A Portuguese term with no English equivalent (montaria, listado, farropo, morouços, terçó) stays in Portuguese followed by the glossary's gloss in parentheses. Reason: the peek unblocks a word in the sentence being read; it is not a reading mode (DESIGN.md § 6, § 9 peek decision).
- D5 The meaning pass is a second agent, never the translator of the same file: reads pt and en side by side, rewrites en where it drifts or breaks a glossary or would make the keyed option wrong, flips status to checked, and writes notes only for an ambiguity it could not resolve; a fix it made goes in the bead's close reason, not in notes. Reason: notes are what a reviewer should know, not a change log (DESIGN.md § 3.3).
- D6 No hand review in this epic: every entry ends at checked; reviewed is flipped as Ross studies, through phase 4. Reason: cac-qgb D6.
- D7 en in the species glossary is the common name as British field guides print it, in its full form where one exists (Northern pintail, Eurasian wigeon, Common snipe, Jack snipe), capitalised as a name; the scientific name is as Portaria 67/2024 prints it, else the current IOC name. Precedent: the § 3.3 example (Northern pintail, Gadwall, Mallard). Rule 6 matches case-insensitively, so running text may lowercase it.
- D8 Translators leave status draft; only the meaning pass flips to checked, so rule 6 binds from the meaning pass on. Reason: DESIGN.md § 4 rule 6 skips draft; a translator's half-finished file must not fail lint.
- D9 Each translation bead wires its own files into the loader (packages/data/src/index.ts PHASE 2 HOOK), so src/index.ts is a hot file and translation beads run one after another; meaning-pass beads never touch it and run in parallel. Reason: the loader test requires every file on disk to be wired, and phase 1 chose static imports over import.meta.glob (cac-eo6 RUN RECORD).
- D10 A bead owns one to four chunk files totalling 37 to 63 questions and works them one file at a time (CLAUDE.md convention); the meaning-pass beads mirror the same groups one to one.

**SEQUENCING**
planned=23 beads in 10 groups, sonnet=0 opus=23.
.1 alone (DESIGN.md). .2 .3 together — disjoint: glossary/species.json vs glossary/terms.json plus the validator. .4 alone: it sets the translation pattern every later bead copies, wires the first files into the loader and adds the translation counts to pnpm validate.
Then the translation beads .5 .6 .7 .8 .9 .10 .11 .12 .13 one after another (hazard: packages/data/src/index.ts, edited by every one of .4 to .13), and each meaning pass as soon as its translation bead has merged: .14 after .4, .15 after .5, … .23 after .13. At most three beads at once, so the steady state is one translation bead plus two meaning passes: groups {.5 .14} {.6 .15} {.7 .16} {.8 .17} {.9 .18} {.10 .19} {.11 .20} {.12 .21} {.13 .22}, then .23 alone at the tail. Hazards: packages/data/src/index.ts (hot, .4 to .13); packages/data/scripts/lib/validate.mjs (.3 then .4, sequential by dep); glossary files are read by every bead from .4 on and written by none of them (CHANGE PROTOCOL). No walkthrough bead: DESIGN.md § 8 and the phase 1 precedent (cac-eo6) rule out a recording; the orchestrator performs the ACCEPTANCE BAR from a fresh clone itself.

**ACCEPTANCE BAR**
Commands a person runs from a fresh clone, with what they see:

1. source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use && pnpm install && pnpm lint && pnpm test: all green.
2. ls packages/data/translations/en: exactly the 18 file names of packages/data/questions, nothing else.
3. pnpm validate: passes and, after the phase 1 counts, prints the translation counts: 506 entries in 18 files, 0 draft, 506 checked, 0 reviewed, and the sizes of the two glossaries.
4. Open packages/data/translations/en/08-biologia-patos.json: 39 entries from id 228 to 266; entry 229 has options A "Northern pintail", B "Gadwall", C "Mallard", status "checked", notes "".
5. Open packages/data/translations/en/09-biologia-pombos-galinhola-narcejas.json: entry 301 has options A "Common snipe", B "Jack snipe", C "Great snipe" (the question keys C; the earlier draft had B and C swapped).
6. Open packages/data/glossary/species.json: the entry with pt "narceja-galega" has en "Jack snipe"; "narceja-grande" → "Great snipe"; "arrabio" → "Northern pintail"; "pato-trombeteiro" → "Northern shoveler"; "negrinha" → "Tufted duck"; "pombo-bravo" → "Stock dove"; every entry has non-empty pt, scientific, en and group.
7. Open packages/data/glossary/terms.json: there is an entry whose pt is or contains each of salto, espera, batida, montaria, corricão, aproximação, cetraria, furão (the eight hunting methods the bank names), and one each for edital and período venatório; every entry has pt, en and note.
8. In packages/data/translations/en/08-biologia-patos.json set entry 229's option C to "Duck" and run pnpm validate: it fails naming 08-biologia-patos.json, id 229 and that "Pato-real" must appear as "Mallard". Revert.
9. In packages/data/glossary/terms.json duplicate one entry and run pnpm validate: it fails naming glossary/terms.json and the repeated pt. Revert.
10. grep -c '"notes": "[^"]' packages/data/translations/en/*.json: the count of entries with a note; open three of them and each names an ambiguity in the Portuguese or a term with no clean English, never a change the pass made.
11. In a vitest run, the loader test "wires every file in translations/en into the loader" passes with 18 files on disk, and translationFor(1), translationFor(229) and translationFor(506) each return an entry with status checked.

**CHANGE PROTOCOL**
- A species or term a translator or meaning pass needs that a glossary lacks: never edited inside the bead. Use the name the glossary would hold (D7 for species), say so in the bead's close reason, and file one bead here, "Glossary additions", that lands at the tail, adds every reported entry and reruns pnpm validate with rule 6 live.
- A Portuguese entry in questions/ found wrong while translating (an extraction slip): questions/ is never hand-edited; file a bead here that adds the fix to the extractor's correction table and reruns pnpm extract, per DESIGN.md § 9.
- Anything about hints: the phase 3 epic. Anything about status reviewed, flags or the app: the phase 4 epic.
- Never widened inside a bead: the translation shape, the two glossary shapes, the three statuses, the group rule (D2), the chunk grouping of beads (D10), this list.
- A wrong DECISION: the orchestrator records the reversal here and in DESIGN.md § 9 and carries on.

**DONE MEANS**
- No recorded walkthrough and no pull request (DESIGN.md § 8; cac-eo6 precedent): the orchestrator performs every ACCEPTANCE BAR step from a fresh clone on Node 26 and records the result under RUN RECORD.
- pnpm lint and pnpm test green from that fresh clone.
- pnpm validate counts 506 translation entries in 18 files, 506 checked, 0 draft, 0 reviewed.
- packages/data/glossary/species.json and terms.json are committed and every ACCEPTANCE BAR line about them holds.
- DESIGN.md § 3, § 4, § 5 and § 9 carry the decisions D1 to D10 (bead .1) and any reversal recorded during the run.
- Every meaning-pass bead's close reason lists the ids it changed; no bead report carries a line marked as not confirmed.
- .beads/issues.jsonl is committed with the closing commit of each bead.
- Each child bead is done when its own acceptance passes, pnpm lint and pnpm test are green, nothing was edited outside its TOUCHES, and nothing in its report is marked as not confirmed.

**RUN RECORD**

SCHEDULE 2026-10-13: added cac-qre.24 Glossary additions (the CHANGE PROTOCOL's tail bead), filed now because cac-qre.4 reported three missing terms and terms.json notes whose combined forms omit the species English rule 6 requires; it depends on .4 to .23.

Species names in a terms.json combined form follow species.json (rule 6) when the two differ, e.g. 'in the hunting of ducks', 'Iberian hare coursing'.

title: Phase 2: English translation of the bank
description:
